strings.d1.theme: Grand Mosque and Qasr Al Watan
strings.d1.s0.name: Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque
strings.d1.s0.tips: A white marble mosque with 82 domes and the world's largest carpet. Free entry, online registration, abayas provided. Closed Friday midday; magical at sunset.
strings.d1.s1.name: Wahat Al Karama
strings.d1.s1.tips: Martyrs' memorial of aluminium panels, with the mosque reflected in it.
strings.d1.s2.name: Qasr Al Watan
strings.d1.s2.tips: The presidential palace: the Great Hall dome, the library and an evening light show (Palace in Motion).
strings.d1.s3.name: Emirates Palace Le Café
strings.d1.s3.tips: Gold-leaf cappuccino and camel milk with dates at the 'palace' hotel.
strings.d1.s4.name: Corniche
strings.d1.s4.tips: 8 km of waterfront: a sunset walk, the beach (flagged area 10 AED) and cycling.
strings.d1.b0.name: Al Mrzab Emirati
strings.d1.b0.tips: Bib Gourmand Emirati restaurant; try machboos (spiced rice with meat) and luqaimat (sweet dumplings).
strings.d1.b1.name: Founder's Memorial
strings.d1.b1.tips: A 3D portrait of Sheikh Zayed (Constellation), lit up at night. An alternative to the Corniche.
strings.d2.s0.name: Louvre Abu Dhabi
strings.d2.s0.tips: Jean Nouvel's 'rain of light' dome and a universal museum, with Da Vinci's La Belle Ferronnière. Closed Monday; book online. Boat tour costs extra.
strings.d2.s1.name: Louvre Abu Dhabi Café
strings.d2.s1.tips: A waterside café under the dome.
strings.d2.s2.name: Abrahamic Family House
strings.d2.s2.tips: A mosque, church and synagogue side by side. Free, with registration.
strings.d2.s3.name: Saadiyat Beach Club
strings.d2.s3.tips: A protected white-sand beach with turtle nesting sites and sunsets. Entry 150 (weekdays).
strings.d2.b0.name: Fouquet's Abu Dhabi
strings.d2.b0.tips: A French brasserie inside the Louvre, with views of the dome.
strings.d2.b1.name: Soul Beach Saadiyat
strings.d2.b1.tips: A public beach; a cheaper option than the beach club.
strings.d3.s0.name: Ferrari World Abu Dhabi
strings.d3.s0.tips: Home to Formula Rossa, the world's fastest roller coaster (240 km/h). Indoor and air-conditioned; book online (Yas 2-park combo).
strings.d3.s1.name: Yas Mall Food Court
strings.d3.s1.tips: A lunch break; return with your park ticket (until 16:00).
strings.d3.s2.name: Yas Marina Circuit
strings.d3.s2.tips: The F1 track: free cycling and walking in the evening, Tuesday to Sunday. Yas Viceroy hotel alongside.
strings.d3.s3.name: Yas Bay Waterfront
strings.d3.s3.tips: Waterside restaurants and Etihad Arena; come in the evening.
strings.d3.b0.name: Warner Bros World
strings.d3.b0.tips: An indoor cartoon theme park; an alternative to Ferrari World (with children).
strings.d3.b1.name: Cipriani Yas Island
strings.d3.b1.tips: Italian restaurant above the marina; a smarter option than Yas Bay.
strings.d4.s0.name: Al Ain Oasis
strings.d4.s0.tips: UNESCO-listed oasis with 147,000 date palms and falaj irrigation channels. 1.5 hours by car or bus; shaded paths.
strings.d4.s1.name: Al Jahili Fort
strings.d4.s1.tips: An 1891 fort with a Wilfred Thesiger photography exhibition. Free entry.
strings.d4.s2.name: Al Ain Palace Museum
strings.d4.s2.tips: Sheikh Zayed's former palace; explore the rooms.
strings.d4.s3.name: Al Fanar Al Ain
strings.d4.s3.tips: 1960s Emirati décor; try machboos and harees (slow-cooked wheat and meat porridge).
strings.d4.s4.name: Jebel Hafeet
strings.d4.s4.tips: A 1,240 m mountain road, among the world's best driving roads. Sunset at the summit, with views over the desert and Oman.
strings.d4.b0.name: Al Ain Camel Market
strings.d4.b0.tips: A camel market, lively in the morning. An alternative to the palace.
strings.d4.b1.name: Mercure Jebel Hafeet Café
strings.d4.b1.tips: A hilltop hotel terrace for tea and views.
strings.d5.s0.name: Eastern Mangroves Kayak
strings.d5.s0.tips: Canoe through the mangrove forest in the city, spotting flamingos and herons. Cool in the morning.
strings.d5.s1.name: Qasr Al Hosn
strings.d5.s1.tips: Abu Dhabi's oldest building (1795 tower), telling the city's history. Next to the Cultural Foundation.
strings.d5.s2.name: Al Mina Fish Market Lunch
strings.d5.s2.tips: A harbour market: pick your fish and have it cooked at the restaurant next door.
strings.d5.s3.name: Desert Safari Al Khatim
strings.d5.s3.tips: Dune bashing (4x4), camel rides and sandboarding, then sunset and camp.
strings.d5.s4.name: Desert Camp Dinner
strings.d5.s4.tips: BBQ buffet, shisha, henna and tanoura dancing. Included in the tour.
strings.d5.b0.name: Cultural Foundation Abu Dhabi
strings.d5.b0.tips: Exhibitions and a library, next to Qasr Al Hosn.
strings.d5.b1.name: Meylas Al Muneera
strings.d5.b1.tips: Emirati breakfast and lunch; try balaleet (sweet vermicelli with omelette).
strings.d6.s0.name: Heritage Village
strings.d6.s0.tips: A recreated Bedouin village with craftspeople, next to Marina Mall. Free entry.
strings.d6.s1.name: Etihad Towers Observation Deck 300
strings.d6.s1.tips: On the 74th floor at 300 m, tea included, with views of Emirates Palace and the Corniche.
strings.d6.s2.name: Al Bateen Dhow Yard
strings.d6.s2.tips: Wooden dhows are still built by hand at Al Bateen harbour.
strings.d6.s3.name: Erth Restaurant
strings.d6.s3.tips: Michelin-starred modern Emirati cuisine, next to Qasr Al Hosn. Reservation required.
strings.d6.s4.name: Umm Al Emarat Park
strings.d6.s4.tips: A city park with a shaded greenhouse and a petting zoo.
strings.d6.b0.name: Al Bateen Beach
strings.d6.b0.tips: A quiet city beach; an alternative to the park.
strings.d6.b1.name: Li Beirut Jumeirah Etihad Towers
strings.d7.theme: Souk morning and a gentle farewell
strings.d7.s0.name: World Trade Center Souk
strings.d7.s0.tips: Foster's modern take on the souk: spices, dates and oud for souvenirs.
strings.d7.s1.name: Al Hosn Coffee Break
strings.d7.s1.tips: Arabic coffee and dates for a farewell.
strings.d7.s2.name: Jubail Mangrove Park Boardwalk
strings.d7.s2.tips: A 2 km wooden boardwalk through the mangroves, on the road to Saadiyat and 20 minutes from the airport.
strings.d7.s3.name: Abu Dhabi Zayed International Airport
strings.d7.b0.name: Cafe Arabia Al Bateen
strings.d7.b0.tips: A villa café serving Arabic breakfast.
strings.d7.b1.name: Mushrif Central Park
strings.d7.b1.tips: A city park; an alternative to the mangroves.
strings.note0: Taxis (Careem/Uber) are the main way to get around; buses with a Hafilat card are cheap. The E100 bus to Dubai takes 1.5 hours (25 AED). The airport is 30 minutes away.
strings.note1: From November to March it is a perfect 22-28°C. December brings the Yas F1 race (hotels fill up), January and February suit the beach; visit the mosque at sunset.
strings.note2: The mosque is free (registration and abaya), Louvre 63, Qasr 65, Ferrari 345, safari 250-350. Tip 10%; alcohol is served only in hotels and licensed venues.
strings.note3: Dress: shoulders and knees covered in malls and the mosque. The mosque is closed on Friday midday and the Louvre on Monday; Ferrari World is cheaper booked online as a combo.
strings.note4: Turkish citizens can stay 90 days without a visa; cards are accepted everywhere; the weekend is Friday and Saturday.
strings.note5: Emirati food to try: machboos, harees, luqaimat and camel milk. Good places: Al Fanar, Meylas, Al Mrzab and Erth.
